title: US Coast Guard Academy Admissions 2026 Guide
metaDescription: US Coast Guard Academy admissions 2026: no nomination needed, age 17-22, SAT and fitness requirements, deadlines, and how the merit-based process works.
headline: US Coast Guard Academy Admissions 2026

sections.title: Why the Coast Guard Academy Is Different
sections.content:
The United States Coast Guard Academy (USCGA) in New London, Connecticut, is the only federal service academy that requires no congressional nomination. Admission is purely merit-based: the admissions board selects the most qualified applicants on academics, fitness, leadership, and medical qualification alone.

About 265 cadets enter each year. Tuition is fully funded, and graduates are commissioned as ensigns in the Coast Guard with a minimum five-year service commitment. The Academy offers majors from marine engineering to government and management.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.content:
Applicants must be US citizens of sound moral character, unmarried with no dependents or financial debt, and 17 to 22 years old on the last Monday in June of the entry year. A high school diploma or GED is required before entry, and standardized test scores must be submitted.

All candidates must pass a medical exam through DoDMERB and the Physical Fitness Examination. Competitive candidates typically aim for around 60 push-ups for men or 48 for women, 100 sit-ups, and a run time near 8:04 for men or 9:59 for women.

sections.title: Academics and Test Scores
sections.content:
The Academy publishes no minimum GPA, but admitted cadets are highly competitive: the average GPA is about 3.79, and the middle 50 percent SAT range is 1210-1380, with an average near 1290. The median SAT Math score is 660 and Critical Reading is 650; the median ACT is 28 in Math and 31 in English.

Math is weighted heavily in the admissions process, so a strong Math score matters more than other sections. The Academy evaluates your best complete sitting rather than superscoring. Take your final SAT or ACT no later than early December to meet the January deadline.

sections.title: Application Timeline
sections.content:
Early Action applications are due October 15, and Regular Admission applications are due January 15. Required supplemental forms and standardized test scores are also due January 15. Early Action candidates must complete the fitness exam by February 15, and admission decisions are typically released by April 1.

The application includes essays, letters of recommendation, and an interview. Because no nomination is needed, the process is simpler than at West Point or the Naval Academy, but the academic and fitness bar remains high, with an acceptance rate around 22 to 24 percent.

faqs.q: Does the Coast Guard Academy require a congressional nomination?
faqs.a: No. The Coast Guard Academy is the only federal service academy that does not require a congressional nomination. Admission is entirely merit-based and decided directly by the admissions board on academics, fitness, leadership, and medical qualification. This makes the application simpler than at West Point, the Naval Academy, or the Air Force Academy.

faqs.q: What GPA do you need for the Coast Guard Academy?
faqs.a: The Academy publishes no minimum GPA, but admitted cadets average about 3.79, and most carry close to straight As. Competitive applicants typically have a GPA above 3.50 with challenging coursework. A strong SAT or ACT score can partly offset a slightly lower GPA, and class rank also matters in the selection process.

faqs.q: What SAT score is needed for the Coast Guard Academy?
faqs.a: The middle 50 percent SAT range for admitted cadets is 1210 to 1380, with an average near 1290. The median scores are 650 in Critical Reading and 660 in Math. The ACT middle 50 percent is 25 to 30. Math is weighted heavily, so aim above 660 in Math if possible.

faqs.q: What is the Coast Guard Academy application deadline?
faqs.a: Early Action applications are due October 15, and Regular Admission applications are due January 15, along with supplemental forms and test scores. Decisions are typically released by April 1. Early Action candidates must complete the Physical Fitness Examination by February 15. Plan your final SAT or ACT for no later than early December.
